blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Threads share a list of 10,000 elements and write to it as often as they read it. Per this page, why is `CopyOnWriteArrayList` a poor fit here?

options.text: Every write copies the whole array, so each one costs O(n)
options.says: The page says CopyOnWriteArrayList writes are O(n) because the entire array is copied, which makes it unsuitable for a 50/50 workload.

options.text: Every read takes the list's lock, so readers queue on writers
options.says: The page says CopyOnWriteArrayList reads are O(1) with no synchronization needed.

options.text: Every iterator throws once a write lands during its traversal
options.says: The page's table says snapshot iteration is always safe: it never throws.

questions.stem: Other threads keep writing to a `ConcurrentHashMap<String, Integer>` of scores. Per this page, what does adding up its values in a for-each over `entrySet()` produce?

options.text: A sum that may include some of the other threads' changes and miss others
options.says: The page's pitfall says such a sum may include some new entries and miss others, because the iteration is weakly consistent.

options.text: A ConcurrentModificationException as soon as another thread changes it
options.says: The page says weakly consistent iteration is always safe and never throws.

options.text: An exact sum of the map as it stood when the for-each began its first step
options.says: The page says that sum may be inconsistent, and that even reduceValues is weakly consistent; an exact total must be kept beside the writes.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: The collection is chosen by workload: plain ArrayList and HashMap for one thread, CopyOnWriteArrayList only for small read-heavy lists because each write is an O(n) copy, ConcurrentHashMap for a shared map.
A total summed over a weakly consistent iteration may count some concurrent writes and miss others; an exact total is kept beside the writes.
